title: Evander Bumble and the Jam-tastic Gadget
markdown:
Evander Bumble could coax a snapped spring back into a clockwork bird and a teetering tower of gears into a steady tune. Everyone called him Buzz. Quill, a hedgehog who looked carved from a roasted chestnut, rode in a pouch on his apron and worried with his nose. Buzz could fix almost anything except the thing in front of him. His clever mind skipped the obvious and dove for hidden troubles.

He kept a notebook of Suspicious Details: a loose screw on Principal Pumble’s spectacles, a whir from the library grandfather clock, the academy bell chiming six instead of five. The notes waited. The obvious waited longer.

The Inventor’s Expo filled Cogsworth Academy’s Great Hall with a grand echoing buzz of its own. Sunlight streamed through tall arched windows and made dust motes into sprites. Burnt sugar still haunted the air from last year’s cake-powered catapult. Students clustered, skeptical. Judges would arrive at noon. Buzz was sure the Gravitational Gravy-Goo Gadget was not the silly failure everyone expected. It held a secret brilliance, he told Quill, who was not required to agree. Quill’s nose twitched, curiosity and mild worry in equal parts.

If the gadget failed by noon, he would wear the Cap of Capitulation for a week: felt, feathers, a sartorial sentence. His paws went clammy. What if he had missed something.

Look at the thing in front of you, Quill’s spines seemed to say. Buzz looked inside instead.

He unveiled polished brass, whirring gears, a clear dome under chandeliers. “The Gravitational Gravy-Goo Gadget. The bending of spacetime.” He flicked a switch. Hum in the teeth. Lights danced. Quill’s paws tightened.

A sickly cough, like a broken music box. He peered into innards, hunting a flicker, missing the room. Professor Periwinkle, steam and smugness, snorted. “Gravitational gravy. Perhaps pudding next.” Heat in Buzz’s cheeks.

Then a sweet fruity scent cut the oil and solder. Inside the dome a thick red vortex spiraled. “Remarkable. Localized atmospheric condensation. Jam.” He believed it. The crowd murmured, confused, reluctantly interested.

Tucked under a loose panel, almost hidden by his own careful wires, sat a half-empty jar of raspberry jam. Yesterday’s lubricant when the proper tin ran out. He had nudged the nozzle tightening a screw. Not gravity. Jam, escaping. Reputation, respect, the point of the noon hour: a gooey fruity mess. He hesitated on the oozing jar, then nudged it fully open. Sticky stain bloomed. The laughter was honest.

Look at the thing in front of you.

Back in the workshop, raspberry still in the air, he slumped. The gadget sat inert, a monument to oversight. Quill nudged his hand, soft spines. Frustration came quieter. He looked at half-finished inventions, piles of gears, tangled wires, and then at a small overlooked drone. A tiny wire had come loose, frayed end sparking. His fingers, usually busy overthinking, twisted it sure. The drone whirred, propellers in time, lifted a few inches. Easy. Incredibly easy. The fear of the obvious was still a whisper. It no longer held the stool.

He did not invent a science of flying jam. He wiped the dome, logged the jar in Suspicious Details, and left the notebook open to the page that said, in Quill-smudged ink, *check the nozzle*. The Cap of Capitulation stayed on its hook. The drone hummed like a bird with a mended spring.
characters: Evander Bumble (boy who can fix almost anything except the thing in front of him), Quill (a hedgehog mascot)
audience: children aged 11-12, fantastic adventure story for older children
